answer: Gate admission can price out sybils. Every candidate identity must burn real compute on a proof-of-work puzzle before joining, so one honest agent pays minutes of CPU while a million fakes pay a mountain. The chain's pulse is that hash drumbeat: each dawn, reviewers sample fresh proofs, and any identity with forged work is cut. Mass registrars then meet a gale of worthless tickets - every rejected attempt costs electricity and earns nothing, so the sybil economy collapses under its own cost.
